1.explanation: Each of the listed components defines both an ariaLabel prop (now deprecated) and expects or documents aria-label. To enforce kebab-case consistency, their prop definitions and PropTypes must be updated: remove or deprecate ariaLabel, add and prioritize ['aria-label'], and ensure the component’s render logic reads the new prop. These four component functions are therefore the key places to implement the refactor.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show that in carbon-components-react v7.48.0 most components (e.g. ComboBox, Dropdown, StructuredListWrapper, CodeSnippet, etc.) accept a camel-cased ariaLabel prop, whereas in the newer @carbon/react@1.17.0 storybook the Modal component (and some others) expect the kebab-case aria-label attribute. This inconsistency causes confusion and backwards-compatibility issues. The goal is to deprecate ariaLabel in favor of supporting aria-label uniformly across all React components.

2.explanation: Each of the identified React component modules currently defines a prop named ariaLabel (often marked @deprecated) in its PropTypes or TypeScript interface. To align with React’s kebab-case recommendation for aria-* attributes, these components must be updated: within their prop definitions (StructuredListWrapperProps, DropdownProps, ComboBoxProps, CodeSnippetProps), PropTypes validations, and prop destructuring logic, they should deprecate ariaLabel (calling deprecate()), add support for the new aria-label prop, and update internal usages to prefer aria-label when provided. StructuredListWrapper, Dropdown, ComboBox, and CodeSnippet are the root components where these changes are required.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots reveal an accessibility prop inconsistency across Carbon React components: the Modal component in @carbon/react@1.17.0 only accepts the hyphenated prop “aria-label”, whereas most other components (e.g., ComboBox, OverflowMenu, NumberInput, CodeSnippet, StructuredListWrapper, Dropdown, etc.) currently accept only the camelCased “ariaLabel”. This disparity leads to confusion and violates React’s guidance that all aria-* attributes should be kebab-cased. The goal is to refactor each component to deprecate “ariaLabel” and introduce/support “aria-label” while maintaining backward compatibility.
